verifications.claim: AOL.com notes that Italy has implemented a strict crackdown on citizenship by descent (jure sanguinis), severely restricting eligibility for applicants with distant Italian ancestry.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'last year’s emergency decree restricted Italian citizenship rights to individuals with a parent or grandparent who was born in Italy'; R3: 'the Italian government changed its laws around citizenship by descent... limiting citizenship to two generations'
verifications.reasoning: AOL sources (R2, R3) directly describe the crackdown restricting distant ancestry claims to parents/grandparents.

verifications.claim: ETIAS.com says effective March 2025, citizenship is generally limited to those with a parent or grandparent born in Italy.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'law introduced on March 28 last year... only those with an Italian parent or grandparent born in Italy'; R5: 'As of April 2025, only those with an Italian parent or grandparent can now qualify'
verifications.reasoning: ETIAS sources (R4, R5) explicitly state the March 2025 timing and limit to parent/grandparent born in Italy.

verifications.claim: ETIAS.com says citizenship often requires proof the ancestor never naturalized elsewhere.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'that ancestor must have exclusively held Italian citizenship at the time of death'; R5: 'If an ancestor renounced Italian citizenship while their child was still a minor, that lineage no longer counted'
verifications.reasoning: ETIAS sources require proof of exclusive Italian citizenship, implying no naturalization elsewhere; 'often' matches the conditional nature.

verifications.claim: ETIAS.com says the changes effectively end claims through great-grandparents.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'The law officially ends the right to claim Italian citizenship through great-grandparents'; R5: 'slams door on ancestral claims... excluding great-grandchildren and beyond'
verifications.reasoning: ETIAS sources directly state the end of great-grandparent claims.

verifications.claim: Citizenship is mostly limited to children and grandchildren of Italian-born ancestors.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'only those with a parent or grandparent born in Italy will be recognized'; R2: 'restricted... to individuals with a parent or grandparent who was born in Italy'; R4/R5 similar
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources consistently state the limit to parent/grandparent born in Italy.

verifications.claim: New rules state that if an Italian ancestor naturalized while their child was still a minor, the line of citizenship is broken.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: '“minor issue,” said that if a parent... naturalized while their kids were still underage, that would “cut” the line of descent'; R5: 'ancestor renounced... while their child was still a minor, that lineage no longer counted'; R7: '“minor-age issue”... naturalize... while their child was still a minor severed the bloodline'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly describe the 'minor issue' rule breaking the lineage upon naturalization of minor child.

verifications.claim: New rules are supported by recent court rulings.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Constitutional Court... rule in favor of the government and its controversial 2025 law'; R2: 'Italy’s Constitutional Court Upheld The Emergency Decree'; R7: 'Italy’s Constitutional Court... upholding the generational cap'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm Constitutional Court rulings upholding the new rules.

verifications.claim: Starting in 2029, all applications must be filed with a central office in Rome, reports this YouTube video.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No references mention 2029, central office in Rome, or YouTube video.

verifications.claim: Applicants must prove "true interest" in Italy, notes AOL.com.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R2/R3: 'requests for citizenship that went a bit beyond the true interest in our country' (Tajani quote justifying crackdown)
verifications.reasoning: AOL notes 'true interest' as rationale for changes, but no requirement for applicants to prove it.

verifications.claim: Applicants face stricter scrutiny of documentation, notes AOL.com.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: AOL sources (R2, R3) discuss documentation processes but not stricter scrutiny specifically.

verifications.claim: The restrictions generally do not apply to cases filed before the new, tighter regulations, says this YouTube video.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'grandfathered in those who had already filed court cases'; R4: 'exceptions exist for those who filed... before March 27th, 2025'; R7: 'application filed by 11:59 p.m.... on 27 March 2025'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm grandfathering for pre-deadline filings, though attributed to YouTube (not present).

verifications.claim: The restrictions generally do not apply to specific 1948 cases, says this YouTube video.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R3/R6: 'pivoted to a court case through Kellen’s great-grandmother... but... generational limit hit'; no exemption for 1948 cases post-decree
verifications.reasoning: 1948 cases (women transmitting citizenship) affected by new limits; no specific exemption noted.

verifications.claim: The crackdown has been upheld by the Italian Constitutional Court, according to this Threads post and IMI Daily.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Constitutional Court said it would rule in favor of the government'; R2: 'Constitutional Court... declared... partially unfounded'; R7: 'Constitutional Court rejected constitutional challenges... upholding'
verifications.reasoning: IMI Daily (R7) and others confirm upholding; Threads not present but fact supported.
